video_prompt: Locked-off static camera, side view. A red ball on the ground launches immediately at 45 degrees above the horizontal, rises smoothly to the top of its arc, and falls back to the same ground level in one continuous trajectory. The whole arc stays inside the frame. The camera does not move, pan, or zoom. Plain flat background, no other objects, nothing enters the frame.

M2_sub_items.measures: CV(v_x): horizontal velocity should be constant

proxy.M2_combination: q_M2 = 等权几何平均(各子项 physics_score)，识别分只在 M2 层加一次（SCORING_RULES_V2 §2.2、§3.2）

M1.principle: For projectile motion launched at 45 deg and landing at the launch height, the apex height over the range is H/R = tan(theta)/4 = 0.2500. Both H and R are pixel lengths in the same frame, so the ratio needs no calibration. The metric is the signed difference H/R - tan(theta)/4.
measurement_steps: segment the ball by its first-frame colour and take the sub-pixel centroid of the nearest connected component in every frame
launch = first frame with horizontal motion; apex = frame of minimum image y; landing = frame where the descending path returns to the launch height (linearly interpolated between frames)

M2.measures: CV(v_x): horizontal velocity should be constant
M2.principle: With no horizontal force the horizontal velocity is constant, so the coefficient of variation of the per-interval v_x is zero for ideal motion.
measurement_steps: over the flight phase, split into equal intervals of 21 frames
v_x, v_y = interval endpoint displacement / interval length
M2 = std/|mean| of the interval v_x

M3.principle: Gravity is constant, so the vertical velocity changes by the same amount over each equal time interval and CV(dv_y) is zero for ideal motion.
measurement_steps: over the flight phase, split into equal intervals of 21 frames
v_x, v_y = interval endpoint displacement / interval length
dv_y = differences of successive interval v_y

M4.principle: An ideal trajectory is a parabola y(x). The metric is the RMS distance of the tracked points from the least-squares parabola, divided by the range R so it is scale-free.
measurement_steps: fit y = a x^2 + b x + c to the tracked flight points
M4 = RMS residual in pixels, divided by the range R
